name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals are overwhelmingly Democratic at D+25
Claire Valdez holds a massive financial edge, with $1.9 million raised and $1.2 million in outside support against no visible Republican fundraising
Open seat after Nydia Velázquez's retirement adds some nominee-level uncertainty
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 97% to win
model.rationale: The D+25 fundamentals of this Brooklyn-Queens seat dominate everything else, and Valdez's roughly $1.9 million in fundraising plus $1.2 million in outside support dwarfs a Republican side with no reported financial activity. With no public polling, a slightly wider uncertainty band than usual reflects the open seat, but the expected margin stays near the mid-20s for Democrats.
model.watch: Any late-breaking negative news about Valdez or a sudden influx of Republican outside spending would be the main way this margin narrows.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Nydia Velázquez's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Brooklyn and Queens seat open, but the underlying partisanship of the district points firmly toward the Democratic nominee. The seat leans Democratic by 25 points, and the 2026 environment adds to that advantage.

Claire Valdez enters the general election with about $1.9 million raised and more than $1.2 million in outside support, while Republican Melvin Rivera shows no reported fundraising. An independent candidate trails far behind financially. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97 percent. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals and the money gap, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-20s.
